description_en: Located adjacent to the Makhana Gaṇeśa Mandira (KAT1502), the Kālikā temple area has undergone transformation, now encompassed within the private grounds of a neighbouring resident as of April 2023 CE. Visual records dating back to 1956 CE depict the temple in an open setting, characterized by a domed roof crowned by an elongated finial (refer to the historical photo below). Presently, the temple stands enclosed by the walls of the Khanāla family, who dwell in close proximity. This family has taken on the responsibility of conducting daily rituals within the temple's premises. Around 2005 CE, the Khanāla family disassembled the temple structure, constructing a concrete chamber on the site, asserting their ancestral claim over the land. Consequently, the temple's precincts were encompassed within their private residence, and the statues originally housed in the temple found their place within this newly built enclosure. Notably, thetoraṇa, as well as silver and terracotta sculptures, which were previously present, are currently absent from the scene.There are no historical records to date the initial construction of the temple. Pruscha (1975, p. 87) gives the construction date as the 20th century but does not cite any sources. His account (Pruscha 1975, p.87) characterizes the temple's architectural style as follows: “This temple follows the style of the square sanctum and dome roof. The torana depicts Mahishamardini. The deity is represented in silver. Near the temple are many sculptures and terracotta images.” However, as mentioned above, the present state reveals the absence of thetoraṇa, silver artefacts, and terracotta statues. Within the confines of the concrete room, a statue of a goddess is enshrined and venerated as the protective deity of the Khanāla lineage, receiving local devotion as Dakṣiṇakālī. The chamber also hosts statues of Gaṇeśa, Sūrya, Brahmā, and the clan's ancestral deity. Noteworthy is the presence of a statue of Umāmaheśvara (KAT1500-007) and Balarāma (KAT1500-009) positioned outside the chamber. Balarāma, the elder brother of Kṛṣṇa, is a rare presence within the Kathmandu valley's context.Given the temple's incorporation within private property, public socio-cultural activities remain absent. The Khanāla family fulfils the role of daily ritual performers for the enshrined deities. They also observe an annual worship ceremony for their lineage deity during the full moon of Mārgaśīrṣa.
description_ne: हाल (अप्रिल २०२३) निजीकरण गरिए तापनि विगतको फोटोमा यो गुम्बज शैलीको लामो गजूर सहितको मन्दिर थियो भनी स्पष्ट देखा पर्दछ । Pruscha (1975, p.87) ले पनि यस मन्दिरलाई अभिलेखीकरण गरेका थिए ।मखन टोलस्थित गणेश मन्दिरको (KAT1502) ठिक अगाडि यो मन्दिर रहेको छ । हाल मन्दिर भएको स्थान नजिकै घर भएका एक खनाल परिवारको निजी परिसरका रूपमा पर्खालले घेरिएको छ र सोही परिवारका सदस्यले नित्यपूजा गर्दै आएको छ । सन् १९५६ मा खिचिएको फोटोमा यो मन्दिर गुम्बज शैलीमा उठाइएको र उचो भागमा धातुको लामो गजूर देखिन्छ (फोटो हेर्नुहोस्) । विसं २०६० को दशकतिर खनाल परिवारले मन्दिर परिसर पूर्खौंदेखि आफ्नै नीजि परिसरका रूपमा भोगचलन गर्दै आएको दावी गर्दै मन्दिरको ठाउँमा आधुनिक कंक्रिटको वर्गाकार कोठा निकाली भएका मूर्तिहरूलाई सो कोठाभित्र प्रतिस्थापन गरेको थियो । मन्दिर भत्काइएबाट विगतको मन्दिर र मूर्तिहरूको अवस्थिति अज्ञात बन्न पुगेको छ । Pruscha (1975, p.87) ले यस मन्दिरको व्याख्यामा यसको गर्भगृह वर्गाकार भएको, गुम्बज छानो भएको र तोरणमा महिषासुरमर्दिनी कुँदिएको भनेका छन् । मूल मूर्ति चाँदीको र आसपास अन्य शिला एवं टेराकोटाका मूर्तिहरू छन् भनी लेखेका छन् । तर उनको व्याख्यामा झैं हाल (अप्रिल २०२३) यहाँ तोरण, चाँदी र टेराकोटाका मूर्ति देखिँदैनन् । नयाँ कंक्रिट संरचनामा खनाल खलकले इष्टदेवीका रूपमा पुजिएकी देवीको मूर्ति छ जसलाई स्थानीयहरू दक्षिणकाली मान्दछन् । यसका अलावा यहाँ गणेश, सूर्य, ब्रह्मा र सोही खलकको कूलदेवता पनि स्थापना गरिएको छ । संरचना बाहिर खुला आकासमुनि उमामहेश्वरको सुन्दर (KAT1500-007) शिलामूर्ति छ । त्यसैगरी उपत्यकामा निकै कम संख्यामा पाइने बलरामको (KAT1500-009) ठुलो शिलामूर्ति पनि खडा गरिएको छ ।व्यक्तिगत परिसरभित्र परेकाले यहाँ अन्य सर्वसाधारणबाट पूजा-परम्परा भएको देखिदैन । मन्दिरकै परिसरमा घर भएका खनाल परिवारले नित्यपूजाका साथै प्रतिवर्ष धान्यपूर्णिमाका दिन कूलदेवता पुज्ने चलन चलाउँदै आएको छ ।

historical_events.event_description: Around the year 2005 CE, the Khanāla family disassembled the temple structure and erected a concrete square room on the site. Asserting ancestral land rights, this action resulted in the incorporation of the temple grounds into their private property. Additionally, the family placed the temple's statues within the confines of the newly constructed concrete room.
